extracted.intended_audience: Mathematical Reviews / MathSciNet reviewers (current and prospective)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting reviews for items in the Mathematical Reviews (MR) Database / MathSciNet, including content, length, format, timeliness, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a review
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should primarily help the reader decide whether or not to read the original item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews may range from a few lines to about 600 words. Well written reviews are most desirable since the lasting value of Mathematical Reviews/MathSciNet as a research tool lies in its independent third-party reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of main results
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should state the main results, together with sufficient information to make them comprehensible to someone already familiar with the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give enough detail so a knowledgeable reader understands what the paper achieves and how it fits into the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketching proofs / main ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The main ideas of the proof should be sketched when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an outline of methods or central arguments rather than full technical detail when possible; include proof ideas to convey the nature of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing technical results nontechnically
rubrics_metrics.description: If the results are technical, requiring extensive notation or elaborate formulas, it is preferable to describe them with a few well-chosen and relatively nontechnical sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive technical notation in the review; summarize the essence in accessible language for readers in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background, evaluation, and connections
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should also contain comments that provide some background for the item, evaluate it and connect it to related items or approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the work in context, indicate its significance or limitations, and point to related literature or alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may range from a few lines to about 600 words; book reviews should try to be fewer than 600 words and should be limited to a maximum of 1500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While important books deserve careful reviews and sometimes longer treatment, reviewers should usually aim for concision (often <600 words) and not exceed 1500 words for books.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to include references to closely related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because MR verifies each reference, give as much information as possible (full author name, title, year, journal/publisher, volume, paging). Include MR Number if possible. References in MR become active links; no special formatting is required on submission. Use MRef to find correct formats/MR numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative tone and documented criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may include positive or negative evaluation; critical remarks should be objective, precise, documented and expressed in good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague criticism. If you assert duplication of earlier work cite specific references. If you believe there is an error, describe it precisely and provide evidence (counterexample, exact reference, or location in the paper). Note MR does not include author responses to critical reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative treatments (use sparingly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two other treatments are possible but should be used sparingly: recommend that the item be listed without a published review, or recommend that the author's summary be used as the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using the author's summary, quote it above your signature to indicate it is used on your recommendation. Typically the community prefers an insightful independent review to either option; if you choose these, put the request in the Review text box (e.g., 'Publish without a review' or 'Use the summary as my review').

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that you will spend no more than eight weeks completing the review of an item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors understand some items require more time depending on length/complexity and other commitments. If you hold items for about two months you will receive a first reminder. If you cannot finish after a reminder, inform MR immediately so items can be transferred. Reviewers with multiple items may require additional time; notify MR if you are receiving too many items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and conflict-of-interest handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If unable to write a review because of inappropriate field, time constraints, conflict of interest, or close 'proximity' to the author (e.g., close colleague or spouse), return the item promptly so it may be reassigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No explanation is necessary when returning an item, but a brief reason helps avoid future assignment errors. Inform MR for transfer; if transferring to a colleague provide their complete name and address so the transfer can be recorded. If the item is a book, return the book when transferring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to a colleague allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: You may transfer an item to a colleague even if they are not a regular MR reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When doing so, notify MR immediately with the colleague's full name and address for MR records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission format and LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are submitted using MR Reviewer Home and the MR Database uses LaTeX; simple LaTeX is sufficient if your review contains mathematical symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your review does not contain symbols you do not need LaTeX knowledge. Many reviewers use basic constructs like $x$ and $x^2$. MR Reviewer Home offers a PDF preview to proofread the review and check LaTeX encoding before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your reviews in final form and always proofread your review before submitting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguities or notational complexities can introduce errors during editing; check the PDF preview for accuracy, including LaTeX encoding. This is especially important if someone else has keyboarded your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the item is written in another language and you propose using an unedited summary as the review, there is no need to translate that summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject classification suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to suggest 5-character classifications according to the Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors value reviewers' suggestions for completing partial classifications and correcting errors since reviewers have read the item and possess expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and handling of provided materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any published material, digital or otherwise, provided by MR to you is intended for reviewing purposes only and is not to be forwarded or otherwise distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are not allowed to upload your copy of the item to large language models (LLMs) or other AI tools; this violates agreements with publishers and may violate their intellectual property rights. The use of grammar-checking tools on your review itself is permissible; MR will edit reviews via copy editors and staff mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming inactive and updating reviewer info
rubrics_metrics.description: At your request, MR can make you 'inactive' as a reviewer and stop sending items until a fixed date or until you tell them you are ready to review again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform Reviewer Data Services to change status. Update name/address changes or reviewing preferences via MR Reviewer Home ('Change My Reviewer Info') to avoid inappropriate assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommending new reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: New reviewers are frequently enlisted on the recommendation of a current reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential reviewers should ordinarily have already published reviewable work; MR welcomes recommendations and will consider them for enlistment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling requests to review for other publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are asked to review the same item for another publication, inform MR if you have already been asked elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The community is best served by independent reviews; if you have been asked elsewhere MR will generally transfer the item to another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to keep the original item
rubrics_metrics.description: Items sent to you for review may be retained for your personal use only once you have reviewed them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not forward or distribute the material; retain only for personal reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel and portal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be submitted via the reviewer portal (MR Reviewer Home).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the portal also to find assigned items, recently submitted reviews, and to change reviewer information or preferences.
